_db_rename_note.reproduction: The frozen DB is at commit ff99bb52326a433375008408004a8db6294a04db; with it pinned, cases.build_all() rebuilds all 1958 cases and reproduces all 1958 recorded instruction byte-strings exactly (analysis/reproduce.sh).
_db_rename_note.validation_json_state_at_authoring: falu2.srcA_class and falu2.srcB_class carry no label yet, so this evidence is directly mergeable.
_db_rename_note.what: While this experiment was running, tools/agx-isa/db.json was updated by a sibling experiment and falu2's 3-bit `mod_lo` (start 40) was SPLIT into `srcA_class` (start 40, width 1) and `srcB_class` (start 41, width 2). The captures here were taken against db.json f5db942f... (recorded in every raw/<run>/00_env.json), which still had `mod_lo`.
_db_rename_note.why_it_does_not_invalidate_anything: The split is EXACTLY the model this arm measured, and the encoding is bit-for-bit the same field. Map the entry below onto the new names as: srcA_class = mod_lo bit 0, srcB_class = mod_lo bits[2:1]. The G17P sweep covered all 8 combinations densely, so it establishes BOTH new fields over their full ranges (srcA_class 0..1, srcB_class 0..3).

DEF-0153-1.consequence: This is a DECODER defect only. An emitter may safely emit mov_imm with imm7 = 12; tools/agx-isa's length rule needs the fix. Do not carry EXP-0140's 'every immediate this experiment emits avoids 12' into the normative spec as a hardware constraint.
DEF-0153-1.evidence: EXP-0153 arm F: the case carries rt=false and outcome=ok with out0 == 12, in both gated runs. EXP-0140 (M4) found the tokenization failure and explicitly did NOT test the hardware.
DEF-0153-1.what: mov_imm.imm7 == 12 does not TOKENIZE under the current length rule (byte+1 == 0x0C makes the 2-byte pair look like the 4-byte 0x?c preamble group), but the HARDWARE writes 12 correctly.

DEF-0153-2.consequence: Any long sweep can stall silently. EXP-0153 worked around it by SUBCLASSING PersistRunner (harness/run.py :: GuardedRunner) rather than editing the shared tool; the fix in the tool would be to treat '' as a wedge.
DEF-0153-2.evidence: EXP-0153 raw/g17p-20260830-run02/PARTIAL.md -- observed live at case 215/258 of D_iadd2_dst, parent at 61.3 % CPU in state RN with no agxrun_persist child of its own in ps.
DEF-0153-2.what: tools/agxtest/persistrun.py :: request() busy-loops forever when its agxrun_persist child has EXITED: _read_line returns '' on EOF and the response loop recognises no prefix in it, so the parent spins on an unbounded stream of empty strings.

device_load.dst_ext9.label: hardware-run
device_load.dst_ext9.range: 0..127 dense (all 128 values), at two independent target registers r7 and r20
device_load.dst_ext9.semantics: NOT a register field. Accepted iff v & 0x1 == 0x1; bits 1-6 are don't-care on this carrier. Write 1.

device_load.dst_lo.label: hardware-run
device_load.dst_lo.range: 0..3 dense (all 4 values), at two independent target registers r7 and r20
device_load.dst_lo.semantics: NOT a register field. An enable pattern: accepted iff v & 0x3 == 0x1. Write 1.

device_load.dst_lo+dst_ext9.label: hardware-run
device_load.dst_lo+dst_ext9.semantics: The pair carries no register information: exactly 64 of 512 combinations are accepted and they factorise as {dst_lo == 1} x {dst_ext9 odd} (v & 0x181 == 0x81).

device_load.extmode.label: hardware-run
device_load.extmode.range: 0..255 dense, each paired with a consumer reading r(v>>1)
device_load.extmode.revalidates: EXP-0141 (M4): 128 of 256, v & 0x80 == 0, R >= 64 silently zeroes; EXP-0141 raw run11/run12 also faulted at 252..255 -- identical, fault set included
device_load.extmode.semantics: Destination register selector, R = extmode >> 1; bit 0 is a DON'T-CARE (64 of the 128 accepted values are odd). R is reachable for 0..63 ONLY: all 128 values >= 128 fail (124 wrong_value, 4 fault). extmode 252..255 (R = 126, 127) FAULTS reproducibly with kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang -- an emitter must never write them.

falu2.mod_lo.label: hardware-run
falu2.mod_lo.range: 0..7 dense (all 8 values) x 4 operand configurations x {fadd, fmul} = 64 cases
falu2.mod_lo.revalidates: EXP-0138 (M4): 98/98 per run, 294/294 overall -- model fit here 64/64, and 8/8 at every one of the 8 values
falu2.mod_lo.semantics: Operand SOURCE-CLASS field. bit0 selects srcA's class (1 => reads 0.0); bits[2:1] select srcB's class: 0 = GPR at srcB_reg, 1 = the non-GPR operand file at srcB_reg, 2 and 3 both read 0.0, and bit2 DOMINATES bit1.

falu2.srcA_class (= mod_lo bit 0).label: hardware-run
falu2.srcA_class (= mod_lo bit 0).range: 0..1, both values, x 4 operand configurations x {fadd, fmul}
falu2.srcA_class (= mod_lo bit 0).revalidates: EXP-0138 (M4) measured this as bit 0 of `mod_lo`; identical on G17P
falu2.srcA_class (= mod_lo bit 0).semantics: Selects srcA's operand source class. 0 = GPR at srcA_reg. 1 = a second class that returned 0.0 at every index tested -- in particular NOT the uniform file.

falu2.srcB_class (= mod_lo bits[2:1]).label: hardware-run
falu2.srcB_class (= mod_lo bits[2:1]).range: 0..3, all four values, x 4 operand configurations x {fadd, fmul}
falu2.srcB_class (= mod_lo bits[2:1]).revalidates: EXP-0138 (M4) measured this as bits[2:1] of `mod_lo`; identical on G17P
falu2.srcB_class (= mod_lo bits[2:1]).semantics: Selects srcB's operand source class. 0 = GPR at srcB_reg. 1 = the non-GPR operand file / inline-immediate class addressed by srcB_reg. 2 and 3 both read 0.0, and bit 1 of this field DOMINATES bit 0.

falu2.srcB_reg@mod_lo=0 (GPR class).label: hardware-run
falu2.srcB_reg@mod_lo=0 (GPR class).revalidates: EXP-0112 (M4) established r(R mod 64) on device_load's destination selector; EXP-0099 (M4) found falu2's register top bit inert. Both hold on G17P for this field
falu2.srcB_reg@mod_lo=0 (GPR class).semantics: A 7-bit field that addresses 64 registers: R resolves to r(R mod 64). Confirmed at 49/49 values in 64..112, including 13 distinct NON-ZERO discriminators (v = 64..76 returned 5.0 + SEED[v-64] exactly). The top bit is inert; 126/127 do NOT fault in this field.

falu2.srcB_reg@mod_lo=1..3 (non-GPR clas.label: hardware-run
falu2.srcB_reg@mod_lo=1..3 (non-GPR clas.revalidates: EXP-0138 (M4): the same formula, confirmed at TEN points; G17P confirms all SIXTY-FOUR (64/64), including those ten
falu2.srcB_reg@mod_lo=1..3 (non-GPR clas.semantics: Two regimes in one field. 0..63 indexes the non-GPR operand file (our bound `constant float4&` was found at indices 6..9 = 101/202/303/404). 64..127 is an INLINE 8-BIT MINIFLOAT IMMEDIATE: k = v - 64, e = k>>3, m = k&7, value = m * 2^-5 (e == 0) else (8+m) * 2^(e-6). bit6 is LIVE here, unlike the GPR class. 126/127 do not fault in this class (they are 28.0 and 30.0).

iadd2.addsub.label: hardware-run
iadd2.addsub.range: the single bit, in both polarities, over 12 input rows x 5 repetitions x 2 gated runs
iadd2.addsub.revalidates: EXP-0146 (M4): exact on 8 rows in both gated runs and 5/5 in run05. G17P: 5/5 repetitions exact over 12 rows including 2^63+2^63=0, 0x7FFF..F+1, 0xFFFFFFFF00000000+0xFFFFFFFF and 0xFFFF..E+3
iadd2.addsub.semantics: 0 = 64-bit subtract, 1 = a COMPLETE NATIVE 64-BIT ADD with carry across the 32-bit word boundary, in ONE 10-byte instruction. Byte0 1f -> 9f.

iadd2.dst.label: hardware-run
iadd2.dst.revalidates: EXP-0139 (M4): identical -- reached r6 at 12/13, fault boundary reg 96, no aliasing at 140/141
iadd2.dst.semantics: (reg << 1) | size. The sum reaches the store's r6 at exactly dst = 12/13. reg >= 96 (dst >= 192) FAULTS reproducibly -- 64 values. EXP-0112's r(R mod 64) aliasing does NOT hold for this field: dst = 140/141 (reg 70) did not alias to r6.

ibfe.offset.label: hardware-run
ibfe.offset.range: 0..63 dense (the whole 6-bit field), in two independent lowerings
ibfe.offset.revalidates: EXP-0139 (M4): literal 64/64 vs mod-32 32/64. G17P: literal 64/64 vs mod-32 32/64 -- the SAME fit counts
ibfe.offset.semantics: LITERAL, not mod-32: 0-31 shift normally, 32-63 shift the field out entirely (result 0). The hardware does NOT implement NIR's 'mask offset mod 32'.

ibfe.width.label: hardware-run
ibfe.width.revalidates: EXP-0139 (M4): mod-32 64/64 vs literal-clamp 37/64. G17P: mod-32 64/64 vs literal-clamp 37/64 -- the SAME fit counts
ibfe.width.semantics: TAKEN MOD 32. width == 0 (mod 32) is the no-mask (extract-to-MSB) case, so width = 32 behaves exactly like width = 0. The opposite rule to `offset` in the same instruction.

mov_imm.imm7.label: hardware-run
mov_imm.imm7.range: 0..127 dense (all 128 values), against a poisoned read-back buffer
mov_imm.imm7.semantics: A 7-bit unsigned immediate written to r{dst}. All 128 values reach the destination, INCLUDING 12.

mov_imm.imm_top.label: hardware-run
mov_imm.imm_top.range: 1, at five immediates (128, 129, 140, 200, 255), each in a PAIRED padded/unpadded form
mov_imm.imm_top.revalidates: EXP-0140 (M4): padded keeps the previous value -- identical. Unpadded, M4 observed the read-back store addressing the wrong word; G17P shows the stores not executing at all. Same length-desync conclusion, cleaner signature. NOTE: in BOTH unlocked gated runs the unpadded cases were recorded as reproducible faults; the 5x revalidation under the GPU lease shows only imm 128 is a fault 5/5, while 140/200/255 are wrong_value 5/5 and 129 is 2 fault / 3 wrong_value -- victims that survived cross-run agreement (see RESULTS.md section 4.1)
mov_imm.imm_top.semantics: NOT an eighth immediate bit and NOT a silent zero: with imm_top = 1 the instruction DOES NOT WRITE the destination at all, AND it changes the instruction's length. Padded (4 B of inert padding after it), the destination keeps its previous value 7 at all five immediates tested. Unpadded, the instruction stream desyncs and NEITHER following device_store executes: the read-back buffer comes back poison everywhere except out[12], the pre-test sentinel (proved offline from the committed sha_0 = 564e3165d8085121). An emitter must treat the immediate as SEVEN bits.
